8-125D. Military Occupational Specialty 125D--Geospatial Engineering Technician
    a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
    c. MOS 125D. MOS 125D is an accession MOS.
The U.S. Army enlisted feeder MOS are the 12Y (Geospatial Engineer), 35G (Geospatial Intelligence
Imagery Analyst), and U.S. Marine Corps enlisted MOS is 0261 (Geographic Intelligence Specialist). All
enlisted and officer MOSs from U.S. military branches (U.S. Army, U.S. Marines, U.S. Air Force, U.S.
Navy, and U.S. Coast Guard) with documented work experience routinely using Geospatial Information
Sciences and Technologies (GIS&T), and having a Geographic Information Systems Professional
(GISP) certification, or having a GEOINT Professional Certification in Geospatial Analysis, Cartography,
Geospatial Database Management or Imagery Analysis, or having a four (4) years degree from an
accredited college/university in GIS / GEOINT / GEOGRAPHY / GIS&T, are eligible to access into the
125D MOS. All accessions must have a Letter of Recommendation (LOR) from a CW3-CW5 in the
125D MOS.
    d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all Warrant
Officer MOS.) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
    f. Qualifications.
        (1) CW2 (WO1/CW2) must--
              (a) Complete the Geospatial Engineering Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (b) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to Engineer
Corps and have full use of both hands in accordance with AR 40-501.
              (c) Have a color vision to distinguish and identify without confusion the color of an object,
substance, material, or light that is uniformly colored a vivid red or vivid green in accordance with AR
40-501.
               (d) Be a U.S. citizen. Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access
to sensitive compartmented information (SCI). MOS 125D warrant officers should initiate procedures to
obtain the proper level of clearance immediately upon notification of the MOS 125D functional
designation
              (e) Must possess certificates in GPC-F, GPC-GA-II, GPC-CA-II, and GPC-GDM-II.
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) CW2s assigned to CW3 positions will attend and successfully complete the Geospatial
Engineering Technician Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
              (c) Successfully performed at the WO1/CW2 level.
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) CW3s assigned to CW4 positions will attend and successfully complete the Warrant
Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Directs Geospatial Engineering Operations in support of Unified Land Operations (ULO).
               (b) Identifies gaps in geospatial information coverage. Coordinates with collection,
production, and dissemination entities to obtain and verify Area of Interest (AoI) source data, ensuring it
satisfies geospatial mission requirements for the generation of Essential Elements of Geospatial
Information (EEGI).
               (c) Projects Standard Sharable Geospatial Foundation (SSGF) requirements in support of
ULO.
               (d) Manages Geospatial Engineering Architecture operations and its connections on
standalone, tactical, and classified networks to disseminate geospatial information content and services
into Army GEOINT System of Records (AGSOR).
              (e) Serves as advisor to the Command and Staff on geospatial engineering operations,
training, policies, capabilities, and procedures in DOTLMPF formats.
              (f) Integrates geospatial data and products into the execution of the Military Decision
Making Process (MDMP) for ULO War-fighting Functions (WFF).
              (g) Analyzes and delivers geospatial information, to include the effects of weather, to
Commanders and their staff on ULO and training operations.
              (h) Performs Geospatial Database Management operations on SSGF data to support ULO
within Brigade Combat Team (BCT), Division, Corps, Army and Joint commands and Tactical
Operations Center (TOC) / Tactical Command Post (TAC).
              (i) Performs geospatial operations supporting the execution of the MDMP and Intelligence
Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB) process at BCT, Division, Corps, Army and Joint command’s Tactical
Operations Center (TOC) / Joint Operations Center (JOC).
              (j) Develops tactical and operational Geospatial Information and Services (GI&S) to the
commander, staff and major subordinate commanders, providing guidance and advice on the use of
geospatial engineering within Unified Land Operations.
              (k) Employs Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), emerging technologies, and integrates
geospatial-automated processes in support of Geospatial Engineering and Geospatial-Intelligence
operations.
              (l) Creates and manages geodetic data of an Area of Responsibility (AOR) verified from
certified surveyors, satellite observations, global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), light detection
and ranging (LIDAR), or related sources.
              (m) Analyze geodetic control or surveyed data in adherence to precision and accuracy
specifications in support of civil and military operations.
              (n) Delivers quality Geospatial Information and Services (GI&S) SSGF data, products, and
knowledge over commercial, tactical and classified networks to Mission Command systems, Common
Operating Pictures, and approved customers operating within the Commander’s AOR.
              (o) Plans Geospatial Engineering operations with consideration to applicable laws, policies,
and treaties with National Systems for Geospatial Intelligence (NSG) and U.S. Army geospatial engineer
elements operating within the Combatant Command’s (COCOM) AOR.
              (p) Develops geospatial Operations Orders (OPORD), fragmentation orders (FRAGO), or
Appendixes as seen in Appendix 7 of Annex B to a given Operations Order or Contingency Plan to
communicate authorities.
              (q) Generates and disseminates highly accurate and precise standard and non-standard
cartographic products within NSG and U.S. Army cartographic standards for tactical and operational
ground and air missions.
              (r) Provides geospatial training assessment and feedback on geospatial operations using
formal and informal AARs.
              (s) Performs duties as the geospatial system integrator on military and civilian networks to
provide GI&S.
              (t) May serve as the GEOINT Section OIC at any echelon.
       (2) CW3-
            (a) Directs, plans, and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1).
            (b) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decisions, and policy makers on
Mission Command operations, training, policies, and procedures.
            (c) Modifies geospatial GI&S web content in support of military and civil operations
            (d) Manages a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) in support of multi-user
edits of SSGF data and geospatial services within commander’s AOR.
            (e) Designs and develops a geospatial Knowledge Management system with use of
metadata formats and standards from the NSG and U.S. Corps of Engineers.
            (f) Performs advanced remote sensing techniques to support EEGI extraction tasks.
            (g) Integrates Geospatial Engineering operations, SSGF data, and products into Joint,
Interagency, Intergovernmental, and Multinational geospatial partner operations.
               (h) Advise commanders and their staff on Geospatial Information and Intelligence effects on
Unified Land Operations and the gamut of WFF.
              (i) Coordinates the acquisition of Geospatial Foundation Data for mission specifications
from supported units, civilian and governmental agencies (foreign and domestic).
              (j) Develops Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP)s or Standard Operating
Procedures for GEOINT and/or Geospatial Engineering production, operations, and personnel work
roles.
              (k) May serve as a Doctrine Writer or Capabilities Developer.
              (l) May serve as Geospatial Engineer and GEOINT Observer-Controller and Trainer to
observe units and their Battle Staffs during training exercises on Army and Joint Training Centers.
              (m) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
              (n) May serve as an instructor at the Warrant Officer Career College and US Army Engineer
School (USAES).
             (o) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
          (3) CW4—
              (a) Manages, directs, plans, and performs duties shown in paragraph g(2).
               (b) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on
GEOINT and Geospatial Engineering operations, training, policies, and procedures.
             (c) Consolidates geospatial requirements from Army Service Component Command (ASCC)
staffs for the submission of an annual priority list to the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA)
for production to meet ongoing and future operations.
             (d) Submits ASCC geospatial requirements to the COCOM GI&S Officer for production.
             (e) Provides senior leadership with assessments and counsel on DOTMLPF geospatial
engineering gaps for an informed decision.
             (f) Serves as the primary operator to manage the theater geospatial enterprise system and
service, integrating emerging technologies and capabilities into unit geospatial processes/workflows.
             (g) May serve as a Writer / Instructor at USAES.
             (h) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (i) May serve as HRC EN WO Assignments Manager.
             (j) May serve as USAES EN WO Proponent Coordinator.
           (4) CW5--
             (a) Performs duties shown in paragraph g(3).
             (b)Delivers master-level technical and tactical expertise on the primary duties of technical
leader, manager, multidiscipline geospatial integrator, and advisor.
              (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
              (d) Support commanders with the development of new geospatial engineer doctrine,
organizational structure, methods and equipment to be utilized in the geospatial engineer field.
              (e) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship, advice, and
counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers.
              (f) Possess special leadership abilities that interprets the commander’s intent and mission
to support ULO, representing and advising on the responsibilities of geospatial operators within their
respective AOR.
              (g) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, major command, Joint,
Interagency, Intergovernmental, and Multinational operations.
              (h) Advise commanders and Engineer Branch Corps Chief Warrant Officer (CCWO) on the
assignments and placement of Geospatial Engineering warrant officers worldwide.
              (i) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform other
officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
              (j) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
              (k) May serve on the Army Staff.
              (l) May serve on the Corps of Engineers Staff.
              (m) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
              (n) May serve as the RCWO of the EN Branch.
              (o) Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have completed the WO Senior Service
Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
          (1) A physical demands rating of moderate (Gold).
          (2) Table 8-125D-1. Physical requirements.
          (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
                 (a) Table 8-125D-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
                 (b) Table 8-125D-3. Standards of grade TDA.
          (4) Qualifying scores.
           (a) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT)
– 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) –120 lbs. and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) –36 shuttles in Physical
Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
          (b) Visual and hearing acuity will meet the standards for E-1 and at least H-2 as defined in
Table 7-1 of AR 40-501. Depth perception will be 40 seconds of arc or better.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
